KNN Accuracy was defined as the proportion of query embeddings for which this predicted label matched the ground-truth taxonomic label. The same procedure was applied independently at the species, genus, and order levels. Nearest-neighbor search and cosine-distance computation were implemented in PyTorch and executed on the GPU. Global class separation was evaluated using the Silhouette Score in the same original high-dimensional embedding space with cosine distance. Because exact Silhouette computation over the complete test set is computationally prohibitive, up to 50,000 embeddings were randomly sampled for each model-level evaluation. Taxonomic classes represented by fewer than two samples in the resulting subset were excluded from the Silhouette calculation.
